title: census-engine-list
universal_lens: The prediction engine unifies sports analytics through a hierarchical Bayesian state-space framework. It maps discrete event dynamics, causal feature selection, and conformal predictive intervals into a single measure-theoretic manifold, treating game states as stochastic processes governed by time-varying latent skill vectors and structural regime shifts.
gsi_mapping: GSI employs dynamic quantification of player value via sparse hierarchical shrinkage and partial membership models. By integrating temporal concept drift detection with conformal predictive portfolio selection, GSI continuously recalibrates posterior distributions over team strength, ensuring robust probabilistic inference under non-stationary environmental covariates.
gse_mapping: GSE translates inferred posteriors into optimal decision policies using multivariate Kelly staking and selective abstention gates. It models situational reasoning as a Markov decision process, applying causal effect estimators to isolate true tactical advantages from spurious correlations in real-time game-state transitions.

primitives.name: Causal Feature Selection Operator
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \hat{\theta}: Optimal parameter vector (dimensionless), P(X,Y): Joint probability distribution of features and outcomes, \mathcal{L}: Loss function (dimensionless), f_\theta: Predictive mapping, \lambda: Regularization hyperparameter, \Omega: Sparsity-inducing penalty term.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes conditional independence given the true causal graph; assumes the sparsity prior accurately reflects the underlying data-generating mechanism.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when unmeasured confounders exist or when the causal structure undergoes rapid, unmodeled regime shifts that violate the stability assumption.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to the GSE `causal/tmle-quantile.ts` operator, mapping statistical feature importance directly to actionable tactical adjustments in the game engine.
layer2.telemetry: Reduction in out-of-sample Brier score and stability of selected feature sets across rolling time windows.

primitives.name: Conformal Predictive Portfolio Selector
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \mathcal{C}_n: Conformal prediction set, x_{n+1}: New input feature vector, y: Target outcome variable, R: Nonconformity score (dimensionless), Q_{1-\alpha}: (1-\alpha)-quantile of empirical scores, \alpha: Miscoverage level.
primitives.assumptions: Requires exchangeability of the observed data sequence; assumes the base predictor is well-calibrated relative to the nonconformity metric.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down under severe concept drift where historical nonconformity scores no longer bound the future error distribution.

layer2.mapping: Directly feeds the GSI `calibration/temporal-conformal.ts` module, providing rigorous finite-sample coverage guarantees for ensemble forecast aggregation.
layer2.telemetry: Empirical coverage rate matching the nominal 1-\alpha level across stratified test folds.

primitives.name: Multivariate Kelly Stake Allocator
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: f^*: Optimal fractional stake vector (dimensionless), \Sigma: Covariance matrix of asset returns, \mu: Vector of expected excess returns (edge).
primitives.assumptions: Assumes log-normal return distributions; requires accurate estimation of the full covariance structure between correlated betting opportunities.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Highly sensitive to ill-conditioned covariance matrices; prone to extreme leverage if \Sigma is poorly estimated or edges are overconfident.

layer2.mapping: Maps to the GSE `decision/kelly-portfolio.ts` execution layer, translating probabilistic edges into capital allocation while respecting correlation constraints.
layer2.telemetry: Realized Sharpe ratio and maximum drawdown compared against theoretical growth-optimal bounds.

reasoning_traces.think:
The mathematical architecture of the Galaxy Sports Engine relies on a strict separation of concerns between causal discovery, probabilistic calibration, and optimal control. We begin by isolating the true drivers of performance using the Causal Feature Selection operator, which applies penalized likelihood methods to prune spurious correlations inherent in high-dimensional sports telemetry. This yields a sparse, interpretable latent state vector representing team and player efficacy. Subsequently, we must quantify the uncertainty surrounding these latent states. The Conformal Predictive Portfolio selector operates here, wrapping the core Bayesian posterior estimates in finite-sample confidence regions. This ensures that our predicted margins of victory are not point estimates but rigorously bounded sets, accounting for aleatoric noise and epistemic model uncertainty. Finally, the Multivariate Kelly Sizing primitive consumes these calibrated predictive sets. By modeling the covariance between different market instruments (e.g., moneyline, totals, player props), it solves a constrained optimization problem to maximize the asymptotic logarithmic growth rate of the bankroll. The duality lies in the transition from an epistemic representation of the game (what is likely to happen) to an ontological commitment of resources (how much to risk). Failure modes emerge primarily at the boundaries: if the causal graph is misspecified due to unmeasured confounders like sudden injuries, the downstream Kelly fractions will be systematically biased, leading to catastrophic drawdowns despite perfect calibration of the residual noise.
